title: 2026 Maximus Foundation awards more than $2 Million to nonprofits nationwide
summary: Maximus Foundation names 2026 grantees and commits to addressing food access and critical community needs.
body_markdown:
## Foundation commits to multi-year support to address food access and other critical community needs


**(Tysons, Va. – September 17, 2026)** – The Maximus Foundation ("Foundation") has awarded **more than $2 million in grants** to nonprofit organizations in communities across the country.


The 2026 awards reflect the Foundation's ongoing commitment to long-term partnerships with the communities it serves.


Since its founding in 2000, the Maximus Foundation has **awarded more than 3,200 grants totaling $20 million** to nonprofits working to strengthen communities nationwide.


Funded by Maximus and its staff, the Foundation's giving is guided by a belief that lasting change is best driven by people closest to the work. Maximus staff nominate organizations they know and trust, vote on finalists, and contribute alongside the company, ensuring funding reflects real community insight and on-the-ground needs.


"Our Maximus colleagues and partners are closest to the needs of communities, and it is a privilege to follow their lead," said **Dr. Arvenita Washington Cherry** , President and Chairperson, Maximus Foundation. "As we continue to focus our Impact Grants on food access and our Community Choice Grants across 11 impact themes, I'm encouraged by the trust our grantees have earned in their communities and confident in the lasting change they will help create."


### New grants and continued support


Ten nonprofit organizations have been awarded three-year Impact Grants of $150,000 each to expand their reach and scale solutions, primarily addressing hunger and food insecurity. A cohort of 52 nonprofits will also receive $10,000 awards for their community-based work supporting a range of issues such as increasing access to healthcare, improving Veterans’ wellbeing, and reducing homelessness.


In addition, the Foundation's 2025 Impact Grant recipients will continue to be supported through a second year of funding in their three-year awards.


### Continuing the mission


The Foundation remains committed to promoting community-led change through trust-centered partnerships, principles that have defined its work since 2000.


For information about the Maximus Foundation, stories of transformation, and the[2025 Annual report](https://maximus.com/content/dam/maximus-com/corporate-pdfs/maximus-foundation-annual-report-2025.pdf) , visit[maximus.com/maximus-foundation](https://maximus.com/maximus-foundation) .
